intended_object: The sequence of Chebyshev-type polynomials P_n ∈ R[X] over a commutative ring R, given by P_0 = P_1 = 1 and P_{n+2} = P_{n+1} − X·P_n. Equivalently P_n = Σ_k (−1)^k C(n−k, k) X^k, a rescaled reversal of the Chebyshev U polynomials. This is taken from the docstring and from "Definition 1" in the module.
explanation:
The body has exactly the recursion and initial values stated in the docstring: P 0 = 1, P 1 = 1 and P (n+2) = P (n+1) − X · P n. The first terms come out as 1, 1, 1−X, 1−2X, 1−3X+X², ..., which is the expected sequence. The file uses these polynomials to build generating functions (genFun inverts P_m as a power series), and it relies on the constant coefficient being 1, which the definition gives.

Mathlib's `Polynomial.Chebyshev.U` uses a different normalization (U_{n+2} = 2X·U_{n+1} − U_n, with U_0 = 1 and U_1 = 2X), so it is not literally the same object. P_n is related to it only after rescaling and reversal, and Mathlib has no definition of this particular sequence.

The definition already works over an arbitrary commutative ring and indexes by ℕ, which is the natural generality, so it is not too narrow.
